title: Artifact versioning
description: Apply deterministic versioning schemes to CI/CD artifacts so teams can trace, compare, and roll back releases with confidence.

data.text: An artifact without a version is a black box. When something goes wrong in production, the first question is always the same: which exact build caused this? Versioning answers that question. It also determines whether you can safely run multiple versions side by side, whether dependencies resolve correctly, and whether rollbacks are auditable.

This lesson covers semantic versioning for binaries, container images, and package registries. You will learn how to generate versions in CI, how to avoid collisions, and how to make version metadata useful for humans and machines.

Semantic Versioning, or SemVer, uses three numbers: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. A major bump means breaking changes. A minor bump means new, backward-compatible features. A patch bump means backward-compatible fixes. Many teams extend this with a build metadata suffix, such as a commit SHA or build number, so each artifact is uniquely identifiable.

data.title: Docker image tags with SemVer and Git SHA
data.content: Tag images so the registry reflects both user-facing version and exact source commit.
data.code:
# Build arguments
ARG COMMIT_SHA=unknown
ARG VERSION=1.2.3

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS final
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=publish /app/publish .
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyApp.dll"]

# Tag this image as:
# myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.2.3
# myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.2.3-sha.a1b2c3d
# myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:latest

data.text: CI systems can generate versions automatically from Git tags, commit counts, or build numbers. The safest approach is to derive the version from an existing Git tag and append build metadata from the pipeline. This keeps human-readable versions aligned with machine-generated identifiers.

data.title: GitVersion in GitHub Actions
data.content: GitVersion calculates SemVer from branching strategy and Git history.
data.code:
jobs:
  version:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      semver: ${{ steps.version.outputs.semver }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: gittools/gitversion/actions/run@v5
        id: version
        with:
          useConfigFile: true
      - run: echo "semver=${{ steps.version.outputs.semver }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

data.title: Avoid latest in production
data.text: The 'latest' tag is mutable and ambiguous. Always deploy by digest or explicit version in production pipelines so you can reproduce any release.

Good versioning is not just a string. It is structured metadata attached to the artifact. Store the commit SHA, build URL, triggered branch, and who approved the release inside the artifact manifest or registry metadata. When an incident happens, these fields let you reconstruct the exact pipeline run that produced the bad artifact.

items.text: Every published artifact has a unique, non-mutable version.
items.hint: No overwriting tags; use append-only registries.

items.text: The version encodes the SemVer and build metadata.
Registries retain artifacts for at least the rollback window.
items.hint: Match retention to your deployment SLA.

items.text: Deploy pipelines reference artifacts by version, not by branch.
items.hint: This prevents accidental promotion of unverified builds.

items.text: Version metadata includes commit SHA and build URL.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: SemVer gives humans a readable contract about change impact.
Append build metadata, such as a commit SHA, to make each artifact unique.
Never use mutable tags like 'latest' for production deployments.
Store traceable metadata alongside the artifact so incidents are debuggable.
data.takeaway: If you cannot name the exact build running in production, you cannot safely operate it.

items.question: Should I version every commit or only releases?
items.answer: Version every build that might be deployed. Even internal snapshots benefit from unique identifiers. For public releases, follow SemVer strictly.

items.question: What if my registry does not support SemVer?
items.answer: Use the registry's native tag or version field, but still embed SemVer and build metadata in the tag string. Consistency matters more than the registry feature set.
